# 1 Kings Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Four hundred and eighty years after the Israelites came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign — in the month of Ziv, the second month — Solomon began building the temple of the LORD.

**2** The temple King Solomon built for the LORD was ninety feet long, thirty feet wide, and forty-five feet high.

**3** The entrance hall in front of the main hall was thirty feet wide, matching the width of the temple, and extended fifteen feet out from the front.

**4** He made windows with narrow frames for the temple.

**5** Against the outer walls of the temple he built a multi-story annex around both the main hall and the inner sanctuary, with side rooms on every level.

**6** The lowest floor of the annex was seven and a half feet wide, the middle floor nine feet, and the top floor ten and a half feet. He made ledges on the outside of the temple wall so the annex beams would not have to be set into the temple walls themselves.

**7** The temple was built using blocks of stone finished at the quarry. No hammer, chisel, or any iron tool was heard at the building site during construction.

**8** The entrance to the ground floor was on the south side of the temple, with a spiral staircase leading to the middle level and from there to the top level.

**9** So Solomon built the temple and completed it, roofing it with cedar beams and planks.

**10** He built the side structure along the entire temple, each story seven and a half feet high, attached to the temple with cedar timbers.

**11** Then the word of the LORD came to Solomon:

**12** "As for this temple you are building — if you walk in my decrees, carry out my laws, and keep all my commands by living according to them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.

**13** I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel."

**14** So Solomon built the temple and completed it.

**15** He paneled the interior walls with cedar boards from floor to ceiling and covered the floor with cypress planks.

**16** He partitioned off the rear thirty feet of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling, creating the inner sanctuary — the Most Holy Place.

**17** The main hall in front of the inner sanctuary was sixty feet long.

**18** The cedar inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar — no stone could be seen.

**19** He prepared the inner sanctuary deep within the temple as the place for the ark of the LORD's covenant.

**20** The inner sanctuary was a perfect cube — thirty feet long, thirty feet wide, and thirty feet high — and he overlaid it entirely with pure gold. He also covered the cedar altar with gold.

**21** Solomon overlaid the interior of the temple with pure gold. He stretched gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was also overlaid with gold.

**22** He covered the entire interior of the temple with gold — every surface. He also overlaid with gold the altar that stood before the inner sanctuary.

**23** Inside the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim out of olive wood, each fifteen feet tall.

**24** Each wing of the first cherub was seven and a half feet long — fifteen feet from wingtip to wingtip.

**25** The second cherub also measured fifteen feet. Both cherubim were identical in size and shape.

**26** Each cherub stood fifteen feet tall.

**27** He placed the cherubim inside the inner sanctuary. Their wings were spread so that one wing of the first cherub touched one wall and one wing of the second cherub touched the opposite wall, while their inner wings touched each other in the center of the room.

**28** He overlaid the cherubim with gold.

**29** On all the walls of the temple, inner and outer rooms alike, he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers.

**30** He also overlaid the floors of both the inner and outer rooms with gold.

**31** For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of olive wood with five-sided doorposts.

**32** On the two olive wood doors he carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers, and overlaid them with gold hammered over the carvings.

**33** In the same way, for the entrance to the main hall he made doorposts of olive wood, four-sided.

**34** He also made two cypress doors, each with two hinged panels.

**35** He carved cherubim, palm trees, and open flowers on them, and overlaid them with gold applied evenly over the carvings.

**36** He built the inner courtyard with three courses of dressed stone and one course of trimmed cedar beams.

**37** The foundation of the LORD's temple was laid in the fourth year, in the month of Ziv.

**38** In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — the eighth month — the temple was finished in every detail, exactly according to plan. It had taken seven years to build.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

1. **6:1 — the 480-year anchor**: The narrator connects the temple to the Exodus — the two defining events of Israelite history. The temple is what the Exodus was heading toward: a permanent place where the God who delivered Israel would dwell among them.

2. **6:7 — the silent construction**: No metalwork sounds at the site. This is not merely practical (pre-cutting at the quarry is efficient) — it is theological. The temple rises in silence, as if the building itself is an act of worship. No violence of hammer on stone interrupts the sacred space even before it becomes sacred.

3. **6:12-13 — the warning in the blueprint**: Right in the middle of architectural specifications, God speaks. The message is unmistakable: this building does not guarantee my presence. I will dwell here only if you are faithful. The most beautiful temple in the world is useless without obedience.

4. **6:20 — the perfect cube**: The Most Holy Place is a cube — thirty feet in every dimension. This is the geometry of completeness. The same cubic form appears in the New Jerusalem of Revelation 21, where the entire city becomes a Holy of Holies.

5. **6:29 — the garden returns**: Cherubim guarded the entrance to Eden after humanity was expelled (Gen 3:24). Now cherubim, palm trees, and flowers decorate the temple interior. The theological message: the temple is Eden rebuilt — the place where heaven and earth overlap again.

— PNEUMA
